source_en:
- The Holy Phases -

New Moon: Cleansing. Quiet Renewal and Planning.

Waxing: Celebrations to channel strength.

Full Moon: Illumination and Power. Communion with the most holy and his Throne 

Waning Moon: Shedding of the old skin. The shattering of the coil. 

Blue Moon: A rare time of Gnosis of Throne and Highest Spheres.

Blood Moon: (This line is scratched out but the last word “rebirth” is legible)

- His Revelation -

Know that the Sun, though glorious, is a vestigial lie. When the dragon’s fire ceases, all that remains is the face of the coldness of the Dragon’s Scales, the earth and the void.

Then come Lunarin and his Holy Radiance. The guiding light in the darkness.

- Lunarin -

Our Holy Lord, Ascendant to The Throne forged from the Demiurge’s corpse. He who commands legions of angels, leads the Lost to their hearths and illuminates our darkened minds with clarity amidst the dark, accursed earth.

- Lunitarians -

Call yourselves this alone, followers of his holy moonlight. Lunarin, our shepherd and the Lunitarians his flock. We are stewards of this darkened land, unblinded by the false sun; we set an example for the nations of man through our actions.

- Resist the Sun -

Though we walk among the day, we resist the fire lit by the accursed dragon, the Demiurge. We who are fallen to this realm are chained to the dragon’s fire. Those who embrace its warmth are lulled into sin. The subtlety of the dragon’s whispers delights the senses, rejuvenates the flora, and was once the symbol of life itself. Through Lunarin we know better, for it's the dragon’s fire that also brings death and suffering. The reaping of its harvest which traps Divine Light.

Clan Telvaught:

Guild of Academics and Archaeologists. Led by Professor Peter Garrus Telvaught in efforts to uncover lost artifacts from the ancient era of The Coil. First to abandon Cain’s Covenant, first to die.


Clan Sirius: 

Founded by Matron Delilah Hexxus Sirus. Traitor to Cain, abandoned his crusade and started a guild of petty cutthroats and informants.

Clan Inari:

Founded by Aaron Chester Inari. Occultist and owner of Inari Weaponry. The Clan have become isolationists, interfacing with Eden solely through market competition providing arms and armaments to various Armaean Kingdoms. 

Clan Harington:

Also called The Pale Rose. Founded by Madam Margarette Harrington the owner of the Harrington House. An academy of wizards and sorcerers in eastern Norundiir far beyond the reach of the Lunitarian Church.

source_en:
He was the god of war, and he wanted nothing else but to be in conflict with a blade in his hand. While the other powers shaped Eden, he marched across it, and his Mahktens marched with him marauders and mercenaries who lived only for the next battle. It was the Lord of Perdition who began the War of the Gods, certain he could take the world step by step. He was wrong, but only just. When he was finally bound into the Abraxas Stone, the heavens themselves were left scarred. He has waited in the dark ever since, and waiting is the one thing he was never built for. The Mahktens were his faithful, less a people than an appetite, gathered from every war-torn corner of Eden. They fought the Lunitarians long after their god was sealed, and they lost. What became of the last of them, no chronicle agrees. They passed out of history and into the kind of story soldiers tell to frighten one another, which is perhaps the only afterlife a Mahkten would have wanted.

They call it the Sundering now: the war that taught Eden its gods could bleed. When it ended, the world wore new scars, places where the sky never quite closed, where the ground still remembers being torn. The Lunitarians counted it a victory as the world bled for their God.

They say that when the stone closed around him, the Lord of Perdition laughed. He had spent his whole existence hunting for an enemy who could not simply be beaten and discarded, an enemy worthy of forever. In the end, the seal gave him exactly his deepest desire. Whatever else it has taken from him, it has not touched his patience. He has all the time in the world now, and he means to spend it.

It is all about time, something which I have ample amounts of. Time for pain to fester, time for desperation to spread, and time for hopelessness to cloud judgment. Man is incapable of truly withstanding the weight of this world; their endless desire for a savior shall be their undoing.

 So I shall save these lost souls; they will have opportunity, industry, and hope. Lastly, but most importantly, something to hate. Each other.

 Fewyl is ready to begin planting the seeds, so to speak, the theology he’s prepared is a sound and almost convincing inversion of the Lunitarian’s premises on the Shattered Coil. I couldn’t have chosen a more ambitious monster to work with. I’ll have to keep my eye on him.

Lunarin is the Dragon! The Demiurge lives once more through the Church. A Millenia of Lies befell man after the Imperial Conversion. 

I have good news, brothers and sisters. Though our forefathers were deceived by the Lunitarians, there yet remains another way to freedom! Freedom from this earth, from suffering and pain, just as we were before the Demiurge ensared our souls in the Coil! The Initiated know the truth about Lost Akyreon, the realm of Aeons Given Flesh, who’ve been scorned by Archons of the Throne. Their unjust persecution is the fate of man should we continue to unwittingly serve the Dragon. 

The Church calls them Demons; we shall call them Shepherds! The Shepherds have given us a gift. 

Tonight we must accept their offering and partake in the powers of the realm beyond this accursed veil.

Mr. Calder —

I have your note. I had it twice, in fact, the second hand-delivered, which I take to mean you wished to be sure I had read the first. I have read both. I write now from the cellar, where I am, as we speak, twenty-three years into the practice of selecting wine for households that pay better than yours.

The Gevreyne of '38: provenance correct. Vinified at Halt's Cross, eight years in my bin. Object if you must to my taste. Not to my certainty.

The Gilded Solera, vault-numbered — yes, I will tell you, I cannot recall ordering it. Yes, I will tell you, the manifest does not list it. I have had a bottle delivered without invoice before. I have not had one delivered without a man.

The Choir's Vintage. You are correct. None has been shipped from the Old Vineyards in twelve years. The bottles I have placed for the head table are bottles my master left me when I came up. There are eight. I have always known there were eight.

Yesterday there were seven. I counted them four times. I counted them with Pelham. I counted them with a candle and a chalk mark on the rack, the way a child counts. There were seven. I have neither slept nor eaten since.

This morning there are eight.

Pelham swears he has not touched them. I believe him. I cannot say I have always believed myself.

I will take responsibility for the list. The list is mine. I am not an old man yet, Calder, but I am old enough to know when a cellar has been entered, and I am old enough to know when it has been entered twice.

Pour from the right side of the head table first. I will decant the Choir's Vintage there myself.

And come down before the carriages arrive. I would like you to look at the rack with me.

— Master Auber

My Mereda,
Oh how many times have I tried to write this letter to you? How many times have I burned the pages for fear of being found by the Church? I know it has been years since you thought me dead. Since I was dead. But I thought about you every day since.
After we won the Battle of the Last Kingdoms, the Church took us in. We thought it was to reward us for fulfilling our sacred duty. But instead it was a trap. They tricked us and  walked us into our own abattoir. We were slaughtered before we could even draw our swords. I would like to tell you that I fought well and held on to the last, but I didn’t. I fell as quickly as the rest.
And yet, I write to you now. No, I am not some specter haunting you beyond death’s threshold. No, I am very much alive, resurrected. The angel who lives inside of me pulled me back from the cold darkness and gave me a second life. 
The Church isn’t sure what to do with me. "Gallow’s Wraith” they call me. I’ll take the moniker if it means I’m able to save the few of my brothers who still yet live. Strange as it may sound, I am trying to work with the Church. Getting them to stop hunting the Nephilim in exchange for our service and fealty to them. I’m trying to establish an Order. 
Please come join me. We could do this together. We will need your knowledge and your critical eye. The Church is overflowing with tomes that haven’t been touched for generations. You would love it here. 
I confess the years have done little to diminish what I feel for you. Please, join me and let us see what we can make of this new Order. Perhaps we shall even find a new willow tree.
Yours,
Gallant

My Mereda, with a heart that feels set aflame by Cain himself, I burn for your touch. My ears can hear nothing but your cooing laugh that flows past your lips like a joke only you will ever know. 
My angel tells me I am being foolish – of course I am. He tells me I should focus on my training. Why would I give even a fraction of my thought on that punishing, brutal, and cruel treatment, when I can close my eyes and see your form laid bare before me.
I have not been lucky in my young life, but finally winning you over to my passions and pulling you away from your books is my greatest fortune. You said we were doomed from the start, but I don’t care. I would fight through the infernal gates and slay a thousand souls to once again feel your body against mine. You may think we are doomed, but from the lingering taste of you upon my lips I know you don’t care either. 
The world, no, all of the heavens and hells are at war, my love. Tomorrow is a promise neither of us can keep. But tonight, my dearest, tonight I can promise that if you meet me under our old willow tree I will burn the heavens themselves with my passion for you. My hands have no purpose if not to hold you. My heart has no reason to beat if not near you --
My commander enters, I must go. Be with me tonight.
I am forever truly yours 
Gallant

My dear Mr. Moore — if I may presume the address —

You will forgive a letter from a man you may not recall having met. We were introduced at the Cathedral Auxiliary’s spring concert, two years past, by Master Felwyl. I do not expect the moment was memorable to you. The fault was mine.

My daughter, Vespera Halhurst, has spoken for weeks now of an understanding between yourself and herself.

I have written that sentence six times. It has not improved.

She is a vivid girl. In her years at the Academy, she has brought home many enthusiasms: poets, causes, philosophies, flowers pressed between borrowed books. Most passed before supper grew cold.

This one has not passed.

She has named the garden. She has named the hour. She has described, with some firmness, the jewel she believes would befit the occasion. When asked whether she possesses any letter from you, she says she has better than a letter, and will show it when I stop treating her as a child.

I did not press her further.

Should any part of this prove true, you would find me the readiest blessing in Gildenarch. You would also find, at your disposal, such endowment as remains within my house. Wassinger & Stoke have my instructions.

Should it prove — as I suspect it must — that my daughter has mistaken courtesy for affection, and affection for intention, I beg you to consider this letter unsent. I have asked no answer. I have imposed no obligation. The matter shall remain the private foolishness of one humble household.

I shall not see you at the Gala. I had not the standing to be invited. Vespera, however, has been beside herself all morning. She has dismissed two gowns, wept over a sash, and asked three times whether a man such as yourself prefers rubies to diamonds.

I told her I would not know.

She laughed at that. Kindly, I think.

I shall be at home tonight, hoping for word from my daughter, and dreading it in equal measure.

With every regard, and every deference,

-Cornelius Halhurst

Preamble

In the name of Lunarin, our Holy Divine, and the joint authorities of The Holy Lineage, the kingdoms of Velchoria and the Nephilim Gallant Alexander, let it be known that this Covenant is struck. To preserve the realm’s peace and the assured continued existence of the Nephilim, we hereby establish a holy order of knighthood in service to the Lunitarian Church of Velchoria.

Section 1: The Order shall henceforth be known as The Knights of the Crimson Moon. All Nephilim within the Velchorian Empire must relinquish themselves to the Order and serve the Church faithfully.

The Holy Lineage assures the following provisions:

-	The continued legal existence of Nephilim within the realm.
-	The highest degree of armaments, care, and security to the Nephilim.
-	Military Training, State-sanctioned education, and religious moral guidance.
-	Immortality through Angelic Technology, Augmentation and Angelic Training.

The Nephilim, by agreement of Gallant Alexander on behalf of all Nephilim:

-	Concede total autonomy beyond the Church’s jurisdiction.
-	Faithful service to the Lunitarian Church of Velchoria.
-   Total adoption of all Church doctrine regarding the Nephilim's Origins, and Nature.
-	Shalt not produce or bear any children.
-	Answer the call of the Lunitarian Church without question.

Hierachy of the Order is absolute and is as followers

The Knight Commander: Gallant Alexander. 2nd only to The Holy Lineage.

Chapter Masters: Sylvia Lochart. Markus Dianas. Yaron Volkart.

Paladins and their Subsequent Oaths

-   The Divine Oath. Protectors of Luminar.

-   The Moonlight Oath. Enforcer's of the Church's Will In foreign lands.

-   The Midnight Oath. Inquisitors and Hunters of those suspected of Demonic Worship.

-   The Crimson Oath. Frontline Defenders deployed at the will of the Church during times of crisis.

Solomon, your absence at the gathering has aroused suspicion among the Patriarchs and Matriarchs of the other clans. I do not know what it is you’re doing in Velchoria, but I must remind you of the Pact. Cain is dead, and it is better he remains that way; we’ve no desire to go to war against the Church or all of Eden, for that matter. Without mankind, we have no cattle, and as long as Cain can’t reach us, we are free to use his blood as we see fit. We have something good going on; other clans do not want you jeopardizing it for your religious nonsense.

Lastly, I’d be remiss not to remind you that you still owe Clan Telvaught our blade Scirax. If you do not return it to us, we may come to collect it.

The South Bed. Asters opened on the eleventh of the Fifth Month. Last year was the twentieth. Year before that, the twenty-second. In thirty years I never seen them open so early.

Roses on the West Border. No rust. Not one leaf. Rust come every June since '79, every year. None this year. I should be pleased. I am not.

The Eastern Plot. Three rows of bulbs come up that I never put down. White, narrow at the bottom, fluted at the top, with a kind of tongue between the petals. I asked Halt at the apothecary. He never seen them. I asked the man at Vellgrove Press. He never seen them. I borrowed a book on Velchorian flora from the Library. The book don't know them either. They opened on Tuesday and they have not closed since.

The North Bed. There is a worm in the soil that don't answer to lime. I tried lime. I tried fire. I tried salt. The worm is in a jar on my bench and it has not stopped moving. When I look at it long enough, it stops looking like a worm.

The Conservatory. A vine of a kind I do not know, putting out a flower I cannot put a name to. It come up between the floorstones, where there is no soil. It is rooted in stone. I cut it on Monday. It was back on Wednesday and longer. The flower opens at dusk and turns to the south doors. The first hour it has no smell. The second hour it smells of a dressed hare.
I asked Bevan to keep the south doors locked tonight. He said he will. He is a good boy.
I will be on the grounds for the Gala. The lanterns want lighting. The torches on the carriage path want lighting. After that I will sit in my shed and watch the south doors.
— Marn

Vauron —

I am sending this to your townhouse, and I trust you will read it in your dressing-room before the carriage. Read it before you put on your gloves.

I have eight cases now, perhaps nine. The presentation is alike in each, and like nothing in the texts at my disposal.

An elevation of mood unaccounted for by circumstance. A wasting of the flesh that will not answer to appetite, which is in every case strong. A warmth and brightness of the complexion — one of my patients, a girl of seventeen, was good enough to call it a lit lamp behind the cheek, and I have not improved upon her phrase. The pulse hurried, near a hundred, even at rest. Sleep undisturbed. The spirits buoyant.

None complain of pain. This troubles me more than pain would.

I have had word from a colleague in Pontoon Town of the like in working men and women. I am told the Cathedral Auxiliary's clinic in the Mill Ward has seen perhaps a dozen this season among the poor. The same cheerfulness. The same hunger. The same light beneath the skin.

The Gala, my friend, will gather every ward of the city under a single roof. Old Money. New Money. Faculty. Clergy. Service staff drawn from districts they would not otherwise be permitted to enter. If this affliction passes from one body to another — and I am not yet prepared to commit to the if — then tonight is a pile of kindling into which we are placing several thousand small flames at once.

I ask you, as a friend, to look.

Look at the wrists, where the skin is thin. Look at the eyes when the candle is between you and the patient; the gleam will be unmistakable if one knows to look for it. Look at who eats, who only seems to eat, and who refuses with thanks. Watch especially for those who praise the wine and do not swallow.

Should you mark it in three guests — three, not two — withdraw from the room. Find me in the second-floor library. Bring whom you must. Tell no one why.

I have not yet a name for what this is. I know what it is not. It is not anything I was taught to recognise.
— M.

COOKIES, MOBILE IDs, AND SIMILAR TECHNOLOGIES

We may use cookies, web beacons, mobile analytics and advertising IDs, and similar technologies to operate our websites, games, and apps to help collect data, including usage data, identifiers, and device information.

What are cookies and similar technologies?

Cookies are small text files placed by a website and stored by your browser on your device. A cookie can later be read when your browser connects to a web server in the same domain that placed the cookie. The text in a cookie contains a string of numbers and letters that may uniquely identify your device and can contain other information as well. This allows the web server to recognize your browser over time, each time it connects to that web server.

Web beacons are electronic images (also called single-pixel or clear GIFs) that are contained within a website or email. When your browser opens a webpage or email that contains a web beacon, it automatically connects to the web server that hosts the image (typically operated by a third party). This allows that web server to log information about your device and to set and read its own cookies. In the same way, third-party content on our websites (such as embedded videos, plug-ins, or ads) results in your browser connecting to the third-party web server that hosts that content. We also include web beacons in our email messages or newsletters to tell us if you open and act on them.

How do we and our partners use cookies and similar technologies?

We, and our analytics and advertising partners, use these technologies in our websites, and games to collect personal data (such as the pages you visit, the links you click on, and similar usage information, identifiers, and device information) when you use our services, including personal data about your online activities over time and across different websites or online services.[1] This data is used to store your preferences and settings, enable you to sign-in, analyze how our websites and apps perform, track your interaction with the site or app, develop inferences, deliver and tailor interest-based advertising, combat fraud, and fulfill other legitimate purposes. We and/or our partners also share the data we collect or infer with third parties for these purposes. For more information about the third-party analytics and advertising partners that collect personal data on our services, please see the “Our Disclosure of Personal Data” section of this Statement.

We do not knowingly use, or allow use of, data from users under 16 years of age or data collected from our child-directed games and experiences to deliver and tailor interest-based advertising.

source_en: Shall I tell you the story of the Crimson Moon? Yes, you Nephilim love this story. Your story. Long ago, we lived under a Golden Age. An age that ended when fell Lord Cain rose against the church. Helpless and outnumbered against an army of dead, the church made you: Nephilim. With divine grace and angelic fury, you razed the dead and ended Cain's crusade. That's when it happened. A new age born under the light of a Crimson Moon. Some say it brought strange blessings: extended life and harvests that bloom. Others say 'tis an omen. A red hue of apocalypse. That's how the story goes. The namesake of your Order. The story of the Crimson Moon.
